Digital Access Equity in Philadelphia

Do digitally vulnerable neighbourhoods have equitable access to city internet resources?

Published

October 2, 2025

Context

Philadelphia operates a network of free public Wi-Fi sites, a subset of which also provide public-use computers. This analysis asks whether the households least likely to have internet access and computing devices at home are within walking distance of those sites.

Research question: do digitally vulnerable census tracts have adequate access to free Wi-Fi sites with public computers?

Data

Home broadband and device access — American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2023 release, which covers 2019–2023, at census-tract level for Philadelphia County. Retrieved with tidycensus.

Variable ACS code Meaning
total_hh B28001_001 Total households
has_broadband B28002_004 Broadband subscription of any type
smartphone_only B28001_006 Smartphone with no other computing device
no_computer B28003_006 No computer
median_income B19013_001 Median household income

Note that B28003_002 is “Has a computer”, not its complement. The no-computer count is B28003_006.

This period spans the federal Affordable Connectivity Program, which subsidised home broadband for low-income households and expired in 2024. Actual broadband access today may be lower than these estimates suggest.

Free Wi-Fi locations — City of Philadelphia, via OpenDataPhilly (https://opendataphilly.org/datasets/free-wifi/). scripts/00_get_data.R downloads the layer and records the retrieval date in data/DOWNLOAD_DATE.txt.

All spatial data is projected to Pennsylvania South State Plane (EPSG:2272, feet) for distance work. There are 254 Wi-Fi locations and 408 Philadelphia tracts.

Code 
library(sf); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(stringr)
library(tigris); library(tidycensus); library(units)
library(knitr); library(ggspatial); library(ggnewscale); library(kableExtra)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
census_api_key(Sys.getenv("CENSUS_API_KEY"))

CRS_FT  <- 2272
HALF_MI <- 2640   # feet
Code 
acs <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = c(total_pop = "B01003_001", total_hh = "B28001_001",
                smartphone_only = "B28001_006", has_broadband = "B28002_004",
                no_computer = "B28003_006", median_income = "B19013_001"),
  state = "PA", county = "Philadelphia", year = 2023, output = "wide"
)

# Select before joining so the join does not produce .x/.y duplicate columns.
tracts_philly <- tracts(state = "PA", cb = TRUE, year = 2023, progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  filter(COUNTYFP == "101") |>
  select(GEOID, NAMELSAD, geometry)

philly <- acs |>
  select(GEOID, total_popE, total_hhE, smartphone_onlyE,
         has_broadbandE, no_computerE, median_incomeE) |>
  left_join(tracts_philly, by = "GEOID") |>
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_transform(CRS_FT) |>
  mutate(
    percent_no_bb       = (1 - has_broadbandE / total_hhE) * 100,
    percent_smart_only  = (smartphone_onlyE   / total_hhE) * 100,
    percent_no_computer = (no_computerE       / total_hhE) * 100
  )

Defining digital vulnerability

A tract is digitally vulnerable if it is in the top quartile of either

  • households without home broadband, or
  • households relying on a smartphone only for internet access.

Thresholds are computed from the data as the 75th percentile of each measure, rather than hardcoded, so they stay correct if the data is refreshed.

Smartphone-only is used deliberately here as a device-adequacy measure: a smartphone is a poor substitute for a computer for job applications, coursework and benefits enrolment. It is not the same as having no computer at all, and is not described as such anywhere in this document.

Code 
q75 <- function(x) quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
thr_bb <- q75(philly$percent_no_bb)
thr_so <- q75(philly$percent_smart_only)

vulnerable <- philly |>
  filter(percent_no_bb >= thr_bb | percent_smart_only >= thr_so) |>
  mutate(Vulnerable = "Digitally vulnerable tract")

tibble::tibble(
  Measure   = c("% households without broadband", "% households smartphone-only"),
  `75th percentile` = round(c(thr_bb, thr_so), 2)
) |> kable()
Measure 75th percentile
% households without broadband 17.51
% households smartphone-only 15.77

Access to Wi-Fi sites with computers

Only sites that both provide public computers and are currently active are counted. This single filtered object is used for every buffer, distance and map in the analysis — an earlier version filtered inconsistently between steps, which produced distances measured to the wrong sites.

Code 
wifi_all <- st_read("data/free_city_wifi_locations.shp", quiet = TRUE) |>
  st_transform(CRS_FT)

wifi_computer_sites <- wifi_all |>
  filter(computers_ == "Y", to_display == "ACTIVE")

coverage <- wifi_computer_sites |> st_buffer(HALF_MI) |> st_union()

coverage_sf <- coverage |> st_cast("POLYGON") |> st_as_sf() |>
  mutate(legend = "0.5 mi from a Wi-Fi site with computers")
Code 
tibble::tibble(
  Category = c("All free Wi-Fi locations", "With public computers",
               "With computers and active"),
  Count = c(nrow(wifi_all), sum(wifi_all$computers_ == "Y"),
            nrow(wifi_computer_sites))
) |> kable()
Category Count
All free Wi-Fi locations 254
With public computers 53
With computers and active 52
Code 
ggplot(philly) +
  geom_sf(color = "darkgray", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = vulnerable, aes(fill = Vulnerable)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Digitally vulnerable tract" = "#7B3294"), name = NULL) +
  geom_sf(data = wifi_computer_sites, size = 0.9) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(
    title = "Digitally vulnerable tracts and free Wi-Fi sites with computers",
    subtitle = str_wrap(sprintf(
      "Vulnerable: >=%.1f%% of households without broadband or >=%.1f%% smartphone-only",
      thr_bb, thr_so), 70),
    caption = "Data: ACS 2019-2023; OpenDataPhilly"
  ) +
  annotation_north_arrow(location = "br", which_north = "true",
                         style = north_arrow_minimal) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8))

Underserved tracts

Each site with computers is buffered by half a mile — roughly a ten-minute walk — and the buffers are dissolved into one coverage polygon. A vulnerable tract is digitally underserved if it lies wholly outside that coverage.

Code 
centroids <- st_centroid(vulnerable)

# Indices come from, and are applied to, the same filtered object.
nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(centroids, wifi_computer_sites)
vulnerable$dist_mi <- as.numeric(set_units(
  st_distance(centroids, wifi_computer_sites[nearest_idx, ], by_element = TRUE), "mi"))

underserved <- vulnerable[lengths(st_intersects(vulnerable, coverage)) == 0, ] |>
  mutate(
    hh_no_bb       = total_hhE - has_broadbandE,
    hh_no_computer = no_computerE,
    legend         = "Digitally underserved tract"
  )
Code 
ggplot(philly) +
  geom_sf(color = "darkgray", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = underserved, aes(fill = legend)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Digitally underserved tract" = "#3F88C5"), name = NULL) +
  new_scale_fill() +
  geom_sf(data = coverage_sf, aes(fill = legend), color = "black",
          linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.35) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("0.5 mi from a Wi-Fi site with computers" = "#F5A6E6"),
                    name = NULL) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = "Digitally underserved tracts in Philadelphia",
       caption = "Data: ACS 2019-2023; OpenDataPhilly") +
  annotation_north_arrow(location = "br", which_north = "true",
                         style = north_arrow_minimal) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12, face = "bold"),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8))

Results

Code 
tibble::tibble(
  Measure = c("Vulnerable tracts", "Underserved tracts",
              "Households without broadband, underserved tracts",
              "Households with no computer, underserved tracts",
              "Mean distance to nearest site (mi)",
              "Median distance to nearest site (mi)",
              "Maximum distance to nearest site (mi)"),
  Value = c(
    format(nrow(vulnerable), big.mark = ","),
    format(nrow(underserved), big.mark = ","),
    format(sum(underserved$hh_no_bb, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ","),
    format(sum(underserved$hh_no_computer, na.rm = TRUE), big.mark = ","),
    sprintf("%.2f", mean(underserved$dist_mi, na.rm = TRUE)),
    sprintf("%.2f", median(underserved$dist_mi, na.rm = TRUE)),
    sprintf("%.2f", max(underserved$dist_mi, na.rm = TRUE)))
) |> kable(caption = "Headline results")

The ten underserved tracts with the largest number of households without broadband. Households without broadband and households without a computer overlap heavily, so they are reported separately rather than summed — an earlier version added them together, which double-counted and was dominated by a term that counted every household that was not smartphone-only as being in need.

Limitations

  • Half-mile Euclidean buffers ignore the street network, rivers and rail corridors; true walking distance is longer and sometimes much longer.
  • Tract centroids are unweighted, so they may not represent where people in a tract actually live.
  • ACS margins of error are not carried through; tracts near a threshold may be misclassified.
  • Site capacity is not modelled — a site with two computers counts the same as one with thirty.
  • Opening hours are not modelled; a site is treated as available at all times.
